errors.text: The hypothesis makes Ostwald ripening and redeposition the principal cause of small-particle loss, predicting increased average particle size, whereas the target mechanism is Au/Cu surface segregation followed by melting and evaporation, producing an approximately 22% size reduction.

It does not reconstruct the element-specific segregation correctly: the target has low-surface-energy Au and Cu enriching the surface, while the proposed Au-Pt-rich core/Cu-Ni-rich shell alternatives are speculative and partly inconsistent with the target.
The operating boundary is defined mainly by particle size rather than the experimentally observed activation above approximately 673 K and its dependence on particle morphology.
Claims about specific binary mixing enthalpies and kinetic growth exponents are not supported by the cited evidence and are used too confidently.
